Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates.

{∭}_{R}2x({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}V
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals in Spherical Polar Coordinates

feedback.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=25$ for $x\le 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}V
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $5$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/2f5814367e44117edbfee704207ef48da2fdb5fa56cbb76b35dd4b0b1ac336ca.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 5,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{5}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$
